blind_spots.blind_spot: Distributed coherence depends on inter-platform links a contested environment attacks first
blind_spots.operator_reality: Their headline gain — coherent sensing across multiple platforms held together by picosecond timing — requires continuous crosslink sync between sUAS/HALE nodes. In an EW-contested area those datalinks are jammed or emissions-restricted, so the 'exponential performance gains' degrade to a single-node sensor exactly where the Army customer needs it. Same architecture-assumes-bandwidth failure as the 30fps crowd-detection case.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The technique was matured on NASA Earth-science flights (news: NASA HALE radar article) where nobody is jamming you.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Aloft's techniques uniquely enable coherent distributed sensing from multiple platforms for exponential performance gains and reconfigurable and resilient operations.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No visible path from NASA/science payload to Army fielding: qualification, ITAR, and accreditation are absent
blind_spots.operator_reality: A radar payload on an Army autonomous off-road platform needs environmental qualification (vibration, dust, thermal), an airworthiness/safety release when flown, export-control handling for SAR tech, and an accredited data path for its imagery. 1,000+ words of their own language never touch any of it — the D2P2 clock runs out while these gates are discovered one at a time.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: 9-person team formed around processing-technique innovation; site copy is written for research collaborators, not a PM or transition office.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: leveraging innovative processing techniques to transform the way Earth observation, tactical ISR, and high-precision PNT data is collected

blind_spots.blind_spot: No operator, training, or sustainment story for a sensor sold to autonomous tactical platforms
blind_spots.operator_reality: Someone at echelon has to task the sensor, read change-indication products, and keep the payload running — swap boards, recalibrate, manage spares — without a PhD on site. Their language never names a user; SAR change-detection output that needs an analyst-in-the-loop is a workflow nobody has designed for the E-5.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Customers so far (NASA, SBIR topics) supply their own engineers; the company has never had to hand the system to a non-expert.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Aloft provides high-quality synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery and sensitive change indication measurements from compact software defined radar payloads

opener_hook: Aloft Sensing's Army D2P2 (W5170123C0018) rides on coherent multi-platform sensing held together by picosecond timing — crosslink sync is the first thing a contested EW environment takes away, and it's the gap between the NASA HALE demo and an Army fielding decision.
what_they_do: Compact software-defined SAR radar (and undersea SAS) payloads with self-contained precision navigation for drones, HALE aircraft, and small satellites.
notes: Stated own-language count ~1040, but the homepage text is triplicated and includes a privacy policy; unique product language is thinner, so deployment_awareness_absence and operator_absence were capped at 12 and confidence held at medium.
